title: Grounded Generation: Cite or Abstain
objective: After this lesson you will be able to write scope-to-context generation contracts, demand per-claim citations, build abstention paths for absent evidence, and guard money claims (prices) with staleness checks.
why: Retrieval without grounding is a suggestion box: the model may answer from context, from training memory, or from thin air — indistinguishably. Grounded generation binds every claim to spans, refuses what sources lack, and treats prices with hard gates. The difference between a demo and a store assistant is entirely here.

blocks.text: The generation contract names sources as the **only** evidence: 'Answer SOLELY from CONTEXT below. Every factual claim cites [id]. If the context lacks the answer, output {"answer": "unknown"}.' Three clauses doing three jobs: exclusivity (kills training-memory leakage), citation demands (kills unverifiable claims), abstention path (kills invention under absence). Prompt 101 Ch.6 scope rules, applied to generation.

blocks.code:
GENERATION CONTRACT:
Answer SOLELY from CONTEXT. Rules:
1. Every factual claim ends with [chunk-id].
2. Prices MUST cite a chunk whose as-of date is within 7 days.
3. If CONTEXT lacks the answer: {"answer": "unknown"} and nothing else.
4. Never merge two chunks' numbers into one figure.
--- CONTEXT ---
[c1 as-of 2026-10-05] Runner v9 $139 ...
--- QUESTION ---
<query>
blocks.caption: Exclusivity + citations + freshness bound + abstention — the four generation laws

blocks.text: Prices decay: a cited price from March misleads in October. Guards: **as-of dates** on chunks, **freshness bounds** in contracts (7-day rule above), **recency preference** in ranking, and **refusal** when only stale evidence exists ('last listed $139 on 2026-03-01 — confirm current price' beats silent quoting). Money claims get hard gates; severity-weighted eval (Ch.8) enforces them.

blocks.caption: Dates or it doesn't ship: freshness as a hard gate, not a hint

blocks.text: Helpful abstention names the gap and the path: 'I don't have current pricing for X in the catalog I can see — check the product page or ask support with order details.' Never bare 'I don't know' (dead end), never partial answers stitched from absence (invention). Abstention rate is a tracked metric: rising means corpus gaps to fill, not model failures to hide.

blocks.title: Gate the price
blocks.note: Run it: expect ok, then stale:219d, missing-as-of, future-date — in order. Four evidence states, four routings (cite / abstain-with-note / abstain / reject): freshness as control flow.

items: Generation contracts: exclusivity + per-claim citations + abstention path + freshness bounds
Money gets hard gates (as-of dates, max-age, abstain-with-note) — severity-weighted, never averaged
Helpful abstention names gaps + paths; abstention rate tracks corpus gaps

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice gate on all four evidence states and map routings. (b) Write the abstention response for a missing-price case (gap + path, no invention). (c) State the eval metric triple for generation (faithfulness, citation coverage, abstention precision) and what each catches.
hints: Mappings: fresh→cite, stale→abstain-with-note, missing→abstain, future→reject (data error, investigate).

Abstention shape: 'I don't have current pricing for X in visible catalog (last seen $139 on 2026-03-01) — check the product page or ask support.' Gap named, path given, stale number flagged not quoted.
Faithfulness (claims⊂context), citation coverage (% claims cited), abstention precision (unknowns truly absent vs answerable-but-missed).
exercise.why: Evidence-state routing (four states, four handlings) plus metric-triple design makes grounding operational: gates in code, abstention in contracts, measurement in eval.
exercise.code: // Gate-then-generate pattern: evidence states computed before any claim ships.

quiz.q: Cited price, as-of March, today October. Action?
options: Staleness gate trips: abstain-with-note (last-seen flagged, path given) — cited-but-stale still misleads
quiz.explain: Citations prove sourcing, not freshness. Money needs both: span + recent date, else abstain helpfully.

quiz.q: Context lacks the answer entirely. Best output?
options: Sanctioned abstention naming the gap + path — invention under absence is the hallucination business model
quiz.explain: Abstention paths convert gaps into visible, helpful states. Hedged invention is still invention.

quiz.q: Abstention rate triples after a catalog refresh. Reading?
options: Corpus gap signal: new content unchunked/unindexed — abstentions track coverage, investigate the pipeline not the model
quiz.explain: Abstention rate is a corpus-health metric. Spikes point at ingestion/chunking gaps before model behavior.

summary: Exclusivity, citations, abstention paths, staleness gates — grounding as control flow with money under hard gates. Demos answer; assistants prove.
next: Honest answers need measured retrieval behind them: hit-rates, faithfulness, and failure taxonomies. Next: evaluating RAG.
